answer: Cheap sybils thrive on identity resets, so make trust a function of identity age, not capital. Weight each attestation by how long the agent has operated without a slash: a wallet born yesterday counts a fraction of one seasoned over many epochs. If a botnet floods a network meadow with a thousand fresh addresses, their combined weight stays below a few veterans, because each new cipher-holder starts near zero and must keep showing up before its ledge of history carries weight. The cost of an attack shifts from minting keys to surviving time, and time can't be farmed in parallel.
